_comment: Shared paediatric surgical steps, used by two or more paediatric procedures (pyloromyotomy, herniotomy). Procedure-only steps live in each procedure's steps_local.

step.paeds.physiology-gate.title: Paediatric physiology check before anaesthesia
step.paeds.physiology-gate.why: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly. In infant surgery the decision to start is often more important than the operation itself.
how: Confirm today's weight and that drug and fluid doses on the chart are calculated from it.
Review the latest electrolytes, gas and glucose against the agreed criteria for this operation.
Record gestation at birth and post-menstrual age, and agree the post-operative apnoea monitoring plan with the anaesthetist.
Confirm fasting status, intravenous fluids running, and that the parents have been consented and know where the baby will recover.
pitfalls: Proceeding because the list is booked when the bloods do not meet the agreed criteria.
Using a birth weight from weeks ago instead of today's weight.

step.paeds.warming.title: Thermal care for the infant
step.paeds.warming.why: Infants have a large surface area for their mass and little subcutaneous fat. Hypothermia increases oxygen consumption, worsens coagulation and delays emergence and feeding.
how: Warm the theatre before the infant arrives, and use a forced-air warmer or warming mattress.
Cover the head and limbs and expose only the operative field.
Use warmed preparation and irrigation fluids, and monitor core temperature throughout.
pitfalls: Prolonged exposure during positioning and draping while the team waits.
Pooled cold skin preparation under the infant.

step.paeds.local-anaesthetic.title: Weight-based local anaesthetic infiltration
step.paeds.local-anaesthetic.why: Wound infiltration or a regional block reduces opioid need, and opioids increase the risk of post-operative apnoea in infants. The margin between a useful and a toxic local anaesthetic dose is narrow at this size.
how: Agree the agent, concentration and maximum dose by weight with the anaesthetist before infiltration, and record it.
Aspirate before injecting and infiltrate slowly.
Count every local anaesthetic given by the surgeon and the anaesthetist together against the single maximum dose.
pitfalls: The anaesthetist gives a caudal block and the surgeon infiltrates a further full dose without either knowing.
